rows.notes: ESCALATE (20 GWh, conf<0.6). Status: GS Yuasa Q&A of 2025-05-13 says construction of the BEV Li-ion plant (in Shiga Prefecture, same Q&A) is proceeding as planned; a search snippet mentioned a Nikkei headline of a delay of up to 3 years but I could not open the article, so not used. No 2026 confirmation found (latest = May 2025) so confidence capped. Nameplate 20 GWh = company/METI plan (electrive 2023, Batteries International 2023). ref_year: company-stated target of full 20 GWh in Oct 2027 after April 2027 start-up (S44); search snippets (Argus, METI plan) say sequential supply/mass production to 2030 - conflict unresolved, 2030 is the alternative (v1 used 2030). start_year 2027 = planned commercial start (S43 series production Oct 2027), not confirmed after the BEV slowdown. v1 chemistry 'lithium-ion' not in vocabulary and cell format not disclosed -> null. COORDINATES: v1 lat/lon (35.308,135.186) are Blue Energy's existing Osadano plant (Fukuchiyama, Kyoto), NOT this plant; GS Yuasa says the new plant is in Shiga Prefecture - site not found, left unchanged but flagged for lead. Operator = Blue Energy (51% GS Yuasa / 49% Honda); Honda-GS Yuasa EV Battery R&D is a separate R&D JV (50/50).

Honda stand-alone EV battery plant, 36 GWh/yr (Honda, 2024-04-25). Paused in May 2025 (about two years) and on 2026-05-14 Honda said an indefinite suspension of the whole Ontario value-chain project is appropriate (Electric Autonomy 2026-05-20; CP24/Global News same story) -> project_state paused (not officially cancelled). No construction reported -> announced. v1 start_year 2028 removed (originally EV production start, now suspended indefinitely). ref_year: fallback, searched - no full-capacity date for the battery plant; 2024 = publication year of the plan. Chemistry/format never disclosed. Honda-LGES Ohio (L-H Battery) is LGES's row (T010), not here.

Panasonic-operated cell lines inside Tesla's Gigafactory Nevada (Sparks/Storey County); operating since 2017 with current capacity ~41 GWh/yr (Panasonic, 2025-07-14). installed basis: company; installed = nameplate (no further phase with a GWh figure found; earlier press said ~37-39 GWh before a 10% uplift to March 2026). ref_year: fallback, searched (publication year). No newer Panasonic figure found (installed figure ~16 months old, under the 18-month cap). Chemistry NCA per TechCrunch 2020 (Panasonic uses NCA cathodes) - generic. v1 announced_year 2014 unconfirmed -> null. Collaboration with Tesla, not a legal JV. One row per site: Tesla's own LFP cell factory in Nevada is a separate row (added, see tesla-tesla-nevada-lfp-cell-factory-united-states) - lead to decide whether to merge as hub if same campus.

Status weakly supported: Panasonic Energy/Mazda release (2024-09-06) says Panasonic Energy will expand capacity and, from 2027, supply cylindrical Li-ion cells produced at the Suminoe and Kaizuka factories (Osaka). Panasonic's site list (seen only in a search snippet, page returned 403) lists Kaizuka as cylindrical Li-ion - not used as evidence. Capacity: the Mazda release gives only a combined domestic figure for the collaboration (10 GWh by 2030 across Panasonic Energy's domestic bases) and METI expansion of 6.5 GWh/yr (2030) - no per-site split, and Suminoe already carries a 4 GWh Subaru figure, so Kaizuka nameplate left null to avoid double counting. v1 start_year 2003 unconfirmed -> null. Chemistry NCA generic (TechCrunch 2020); not verified specifically for Kaizuka.

Opened July 2025, mass production of 2170 cells; plan ~32 GWh/yr 'in the future' (Panasonic). Ramp is slower than planned: Feb 2026 two lines running + two new lines starting, 'ramp to ~50% in the next few months', construction begun on a second wing of which two of four lines run in 2027 (S5); June 2026 Panasonic says four production lines in operation, ramp to full capacity delayed (S4), EV ramp depends on customer demand; June 2026 investor event: some lines to be converted to data-centre cells from FY2028/29 while EV production continues (HPPR/KCUR) - could reduce EV-cell nameplate later. installed_capacity_gwh left null: no source gives GWh for the lines running (line count only). ref_year: fallback, searched (publication year of Panasonic's 32 GWh statement, no full-capacity date; a Japanese-media target of March 2027 reported by InsideEVs search snippet is now delayed). Chemistry NCA generic (TechCrunch 2020); Panasonic release says 2170 cylindrical. v1 announced_year 2022 unconfirmed -> null.

Subaru/Panasonic Energy jointly established plant in Oizumi, Gunma; production from fiscal 2028 (S12); METI-approved plan 16 GWh/yr by 2030 (S14); with Suminoe (4 GWh) the two Japanese bases reach 20 GWh by 2030 (S11). Status announced: Gunma prefecture shows only environmental-assessment steps (methods document Nov 2024, assessment report viewing 2025-11-04 to 2025-12-03, S16); no construction start found (search 2026-11). v1 'under_construction' not supported. No 2026 news found; 4680/2170 not specified in the release. Chemistry not disclosed -> null (v1 free text). Subaru is co-establisher (jv_partners).

Existing Panasonic Energy cylindrical-cell plant in Osaka. Status: May 2026 report says some production lines at Suminoe were repurposed for data-centre power storage (S7) - production exists. Plans: automotive cylindrical Li-ion from fiscal 2027 for Subaru, 4 GWh at Suminoe (S13, S15), part of 20 GWh by 2030 across Suminoe+Oizumi (S11); the Mazda collaboration also names Suminoe+Kaizuka (10 GWh by 2030 across domestic bases, S17) - per-site split not disclosed, only the Subaru 4 GWh is attributed here; possible overlap with Mazda volumes unresolved. installed null (existing consumer/auto output not disclosed). v1 start_year 2010 unconfirmed -> null; v1 NCA chemistry not confirmed for Suminoe -> null. COORDINATES: v1 lat/lon (36.26,139.43) are Oizumi's, wrong for Suminoe-ku, Osaka; site not found - lead should fix (Suminoe is in Osaka). end_market mixed: automotive (Subaru/Mazda) plus data-centre storage lines.

ESCALATE (10 GWh, conf<0.6). 4680 mother-factory lines at Wakayama: two dedicated lines built in FY2023 (S6), 'ready for mass production' Sept 2024 pending final evaluation (S9), then mass production postponed again - Nikkei/Automotive World May 2026: missed end-March 2026 target, still waiting for the main customer's purchase order, expansion plans on hold (S6, S8). So lines exist but commercial 4680 production has not started -> status under_construction (not operational), project_state paused, start_year null (v1 2025 wrong), installed null. Nameplate 10 GWh is only a Nikkei-sourced estimate reported by InsideEVs (S10) - Panasonic never disclosed capacity; not independently confirmed. ref_year 2022 = fallback (publication year of the plan). Wakayama also historically produced other cells since 1991 (not quantified, not counted). Chemistry NCA generic (TechCrunch 2020), 4680-specific chemistry not stated.

PPES (Toyota 51% / Panasonic 49%) Himeji plant: prismatic Li-ion for BEV/PHEV; new BEV line in mass production since Jan 2025 (S18). PPES history page: phased expansions 80,000 BEVs/yr (2021), +7 GWh/yr (start planned 2024), and next-generation performance batteries from 2026 with 'total capacity of Himeji expected to reach approx. 30GWh' (S19, S20; same company, two pages). The Toyota/PPES METI-certified plan lists 9 GWh/yr for next-gen performance batteries from 2026 (acnnewswire/Toyota release 2024-09-06, snippet-level). installed_capacity null: no commissioned-GWh figure published. ref_year: fallback, searched - the 30 GWh is tied to 'after next-gen production begins' (from 2026) with no year; publication year 2024 used. v1 chemistry 'NMC' not confirmed -> null; v1 start_year 2025 is the new model's launch, plant start unconfirmed -> null.

PPES history page: Tokushima line announced Oct 2020, 'Production has started in 2022', supply of approx. 500,000 HEVs per year (vehicle count; no GWh equivalent published, so nameplate/installed null). Prismatic Li-ion for hybrids (PPES news 2020-10-06). v1 chemistry NMC not confirmed -> null. Small/mid plant; kept at 0.65.

BIG CHANGE vs v1 (100 GWh): Tesla's Q3 2026 Update (Oct 21, 2026) table 'Battery Cell Manufacturing Annual Capacity' lists Texas 4680 at >40 GWh, status Production (slide is image-only; TeslaNorth article quotes the same figure in text, S34). Tesla footnote: installed capacity is not the current production rate and may be limited. installed basis: company. Nameplate set = 40 (the stated floor) because no published GWh plan above it: the v1 100 GWh was Musk's 2020 Battery Day aspiration (excluded per D-015); Tesla's cell director says Giga Texas 'will soon become the largest battery cell manufacturing facility in North America' via a 'massive expansion' with no GWh/date (2026-11-09) - so nameplate may be higher later. ref_year: fallback, searched (publication year). Tesla says 4680 output supports Cybercab, Semi and Model Y ramps. Cathode materials plant (10 GWh early ramp) is not a cell line. v1 capacity_by_year_json (5/7 GWh) was production milestones, not capacity -> null. v1 start_year 2022 and chemistry (NMC/NCA) not confirmed in open sources I could open -> null.

Plant manager (LinkedIn, via electrive 2026-05-13): the extra ~$250M investment 'will enable 18GWh of annual 4680 cell production'; earlier 8 GWh plan had production scheduled for H1 2027. Tesla's Q3 2026 Update capacity table lists Berlin 4680 as 'Construction' with no capacity (S33; image-only slide). v1 claim of pilot cells made 12 May 2026 not confirmed by the electrive page (it only mentions 4680 cells made in Austin) -> not used; no installed capacity. ref_year: fallback, searched (publication year 2026) - no full-capacity date stated; start of production H1 2027 is a start not a ramp-complete date. v1 chemistry 'NMC' not confirmed -> null; v1 announced_year unconfirmed -> null. Same site as the vehicle plant; one row.

Toyota Battery Co. (ex-PEVE, HQ Kosai, Shizuoka; wholly-owned by Toyota since March 2024). Toyota (2024-03-05) says PEVE mass-produces HEV batteries and plans BEV/PHEV batteries; Toyota Times (2024-10-04) places the relaunch event at 'Kosai Battery Park (Arai Plant)' (S32). The company-level statement does not break out Kosai vs Miyagi and no GWh capacity is published in any open source I could open (peve.jp returned 503; toyota-battery.co.jp not reachable from this session). Hence capacity/start_year null, confidence 0.45. Product mix NiMH + Li-ion per Wikipedia pointer only (not vocabulary-clean) -> chemistry null. v1 prismatic format unconfirmed -> null. Arai plant (new Li-ion plant under construction 2022) may be a distinct site from older Kosai factory - unresolved.

Miyagi (Taiwa) site: only a 2018 trade report (PEVE building two new Li-ion factories on existing Miyagi premises, ~200,000 batteries/yr each, 2019-2021) plus Toyota's 2024 statement that PEVE mass-produces HEV batteries; no current site-level confirmation or GWh figure found. v1 coordinates (35.08,137.15) are Toyota City, not Miyagi - flagged, not changed (site not found). v1 start_year 2010 unconfirmed -> null. Consider merging with Kosai as one operator-level entity only if lead wants; left separate.

Toyota plans a Li-ion BEV cell plant at Shin-Matsuyama Seaside Industrial Park, Kanda (Fukuoka), operator Primearth/Toyota Battery (S30, July 2024). Postponed a second time in Nov 2025: not scrapped, about a year of review, original start 2028, no new date; some output may shift to vehicles/components (S29). No capacity ever stated -> null. No 2026 update found (searched English; Japanese search not conclusive) - review period ends about now, status may change. v1 chemistry free text -> null.

ESCALATE (30 GWh, conf<0.6; cell-vs-module question). Toyota (2025-11-12): production started; plant 'will house 14 battery production lines supporting HEVs'; 'can produce 30 GWh annually at full capacity'; additional lines to launch by 2030. Currently ships HEV modules to Kentucky and Alabama (electrive/electrek). I could NOT establish from any open page whether cells are manufactured on site or whether Liberty assembles modules/packs from cells made elsewhere (Toyota's 2021 announcement speaks of 'battery pack output'; electrive says the plant will assemble battery packs) - if modules/packs only, this is not a cell plant and lead should consider flagging is_cell_manufacturer. How many of the 14 lines run today and any installed GWh: not published -> installed null. ref_year 2030 from 'additional lines by 2030' (ambiguous whether 30 GWh needs those lines; TechCrunch 2023 reported 30 GWh by 2030). v1 jv_partners (TMNA/Toyota Tsusho), announced_year, 'mixed' end market and 'lithium-ion' chemistry not confirmed/vocabulary -> null/EV.

Status unconfirmed (<=0.4). Toyota Times (2023-10-02): Teiho is Toyota's production-engineering/start-up plant (equipment design to installation at mass-production plants); it hosts a prototype all-solid-state battery line and prepares for mass production, aiming at commercialisation in 2027-2028. That is pilot/prototype activity, not commercial cell production; no capacity published. Recommend lead consider removal as 'not_cell'/pilot (I kept it as an update because a prototype cell line exists and removal needs positive evidence). v1 'operational' not supported -> null; v1 coordinates are Toyota City centroid.

Candidate T026 (Tesla Sparks LFP line) verified. Tesla's own LFP cell factory in Nevada (CATL-sourced equipment; cells for Megapack). Q3 2026 Update (Oct 21, 2026): Nevada LFP battery cell capacity 7 GWh, status Early Ramp (slide is image-only); first Megapacks built solely with Tesla LFP cells shipped in Q3 2026 (S38, S39). Nameplate 10 GWh/yr = Tesla's stated plan (Q2 2025 reporting, S37; 'about 10 GWh' per Electrek 2025-07-01); ref_year fallback (publication year 2025) - no full-capacity date. Tesla footnote: installed capacity is not current production rate. SAME CAMPUS QUESTION: Tesla says only 'Nevada'; this is a Tesla-operated LFP prismatic-cell plant separate from Panasonic's NCA cylindrical lines (different operator, product, building) but probably on the Gigafactory Nevada / Sparks campus - I could not confirm the exact site, so kept as its own row (no coordinates); lead may merge as a hub if desired. Cell format not stated (likely prismatic) -> null.

Candidate T027 verified: Nissan signed the site agreement with Fukuoka/Kitakyushu in Jan 2025 (5 GWh/yr LFP, operation 2028; electrive 2025-01-22) but cancelled construction on 2025-05-09 as part of Re:Nissan (electrive; also Reuters/Argus/Just Auto in search). Never started -> announced + cancelled. ref_year 2025 = fallback (publication year). Added only so the cancelled project is not re-discovered as live; capacity must not count in aggregates. No coordinates (Hibikinada, Wakamatsu Ward per other press; not fetched).
